messages:
cassie_pm: RFC + PRD sketch in the drive: https://redwood-internal/drive/rfc/runtime-kernel-kv
cassie_pm: Quick sync — we need to prioritize kernel-selection changes vs KV cache TTL work this quarter. Goals: reduce P99 for short-seq (<128) by 15%, avoid regression for long-seq, and give customers per-tenant KV overrides.
piotr: read. Are we combining kernel opt into single rollout or split? my +1 for split: kernel first (lower blast radius), KV policy second.
maya: perf impact depends on attention opt landing. If we include the attention mem-compression patch, short-seq improves a lot but we must test long-seq memory path.
alex_r: infra constraints: dedicated nodes need driver updates; that's a 2-week freeze window to coordinate with cloud partners. planning note: driver bump = ops schedule hit.
cassie_pm: acceptance criteria proposal:
- perf: P99 latency short-seq -15% vs baseline
- correctness: no >1% increase in token-level decoding errors or divergence vs baseline eval set
- reliability: no >1% increase in server errors (5xx)
- rollout metric: canary at 10% traffic for 48h with automated health checks
- rollback triggers: latency/regression above threshold or error spikes >5%
piotr: edge cases we must capture:
- mixed fleet (fp16 vs int8) -> kernel selection must be model-variant-aware and avoid picking incompatible kernels
- seq-length transitions mid-request (streaming) -> ensure KV cache indexing still valid
- legacy pinned configs from customers -> treat as override, not auto-select
piotr: propose config snippet for RFC (sketch):
```
kernel_policy:
  mode: "auto" # [auto, pinned]
  fallback: ["int8", "fp16"]
  prefer_latency: true
kv_policy:
  per_tenant_ttl: true
  default_ttl_s: 300
  fallback_ttl_s: 60
```
jun_ops: oncall note: ensure tracing tags set to `kernel_variant`, `kv_ttl_source`, and `canary_group` so SRE can slice incidents quickly. Also add alert if canary error rate > 2x baseline.
diego: a few customers already asked for deterministic output when we switch kernels. we need a short doc describing possible small output diffs and mitigation (pinning + roll-forward tests).
maya: tests: add regression evals covering our prompt set + randomized seeds, sequence lengths up to 2048, and a small adversarial example set for hallucination checks. perf harness should run short/medium/long bins.
piotr: scope negotiation: split into two PRDs to keep risk small:
A) Kernel-selection runtime + rollout hooks + metrics (target Q2 deliverable)
B) KV per-tenant policy + admin UI + migration plan (follow-up)
cassie_pm: timeline ask: target beta for A: 2026-05-20. can the team commit?
alex_r: driver freeze moves earliest beta to 2026-05-27 unless we adopt a hotpatch path for hosted-only. that adds complexity but possible.
piotr: i'll draft RFC A today and include acceptance criteria, rollout/canary playbook, and a short runbook for rollback. tagging @eng-sre in the doc.
deploy-bot: CI build passed for branch runtime-kernel-opt (build #4523) :white_check_mark:
cassie_pm: please @eng-sre for the canary runbook when the draft is posted. thx :thumbsup:
_notes: This thread captures PRD/RFC scoping for runtime changes: kernel-selection vs KV policy. Contains acceptance criteria, edge cases, config sketch, timeline and rollout planning.
